Basic Constructions
===================
We currently need duration and starting configuration of the epidemic, together 
with two rate parameters. Note following also works for `initial = SIR(0.0, 3, 2, 0)`.
```{julia}
const duration = 5.0 ; const initial  = SIR(0.0, 4, 1, 0) ;
α=0.2 ; β=0.1 ;
```
When constructing `Innovation` or an `Evolution` (or even a `CEvolution` as is given later)
it is useful to use some abbreviations for various `AbstractIncidents`.
```{julia}
AI = AbstractInfection; I = Infection; P = PInfection; NF  = NoFlyInfection; XI = ExpungedInfection;
AR = AbstractRemoval;   R = Removal;   C = CRemoval;   KI = KilledInfection; KR = KilledRemoval;
```
Here is the random seed.
```{julia}
Random.seed!(43) ;
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
using Logging
debuglogger = ConsoleLogger(stderr, Logging.Info)
global_logger(debuglogger) ;
```

Minimal and maximal initial `CEvolution`s
-----------------------------------------
The initial `CEvolution` can be _maximal_ or _minimal_; the definition depends on
the times of the `CRemoval`s, which are supplied as a vector of times. 
We require an `initial` state (of which only the fields `t` and `n` matter),
`duration`,
and a list of `CRemoval` times. Here are functions to generate the `CEvolution`s.
```{julia}
function maximal_evolution(initial::SIR, duration::S, 
        times::Vector{T}) ::CEvolution where {S,T <: Real}
    beginning = initial.t
    population = initial.n
    infections = I[I(beginning,i,i+1) for i ∈ 1:(population-1)]
    cremovals  = C[C(t, population) for t in times]
    return CEvolution(initial, infections ∪ cremovals)
end ;
function minimal_evolution(initial::SIR, duration::S, 
        times::Vector{T})::CEvolution where {S,T <: Real}
    beginning = initial.t
    population = initial.n
    sort(deepcopy(times))
    infections = I[I(times[i],i,i+1) for i ∈ 1:(length(times)-1)]
    cremovals  = C[C(t, i) for (i, t) in enumerate(times)]
    return CEvolution(initial, infections ∪ cremovals)
end ;
```

Working with a list of `CRemoval` times,
```{julia}
initial_cremoval_times = [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0]
println(initial_cremoval_times)
```
we obtain
```{julia}
max_ev = maximal_evolution(initial, duration, initial_cremoval_times)
min_ev = minimal_evolution(initial, duration, initial_cremoval_times)
println("Initial maximal `CEvolution` ", sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), max_ev))
println("Initial minimal `CEvolution` ", sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), min_ev))
```

A suitable `Innovation`
-----------------------
We work with the following (randomly generated, determined by seed) innovation:
```{julia}
iv_null  = Innovation(initial.n, I[], R[], min_ev.cremovals)
iv0 = generate_innovation(iv_null, duration, α=α, β=β)
```

Evaluation of new `CEvolution`
==============================
Here is the resulting `CEvolution` generated using `max_ev`.
```{julia}
ev = CEvolution(max_ev, iv0)
```
The resulting `LFE` is
```{julia}
ev.LFE
```
**ISSUE:** original implementation of 
`LFE` does not report perpetuation! 

Towards a correct and robust generation of `LFE`
================================================
We work with the `CEvolution` given by `ev = CEvolution(max_ev, iv0)`.

The resulting underlying chronology is
```{julia}
ev.chronology
```

The `KilledInfection`s are those which have `target` field at or below the removal boundary.
The removal boundary for each of the `AbstractIncident`s in the chronology can be computed 
as follows, and used to check correctness of categorization of `KilledInfection`s.
So we can remove all `KilledInfection`s (we do _not_ remove `KilledRemoval`s).
```{julia}
removal_boundary =
    accumulate(+, z isa CRemoval ? 1 : 0 for z in ev.chronology, init=initial.r)
@test any(z isa KilledInfection ? z.target ≤ rb : z.target > rb for 
    (z, rb) in zip(ev.chronology, removal_boundary)) ;
relevant_chronology =
    filter(z -> !(z isa KilledInfection), ev.chronology)
```
Note `ev_reduced` has the same trajectory and history as the full `ev`!
```{julia}
ev_reduced = CEvolution(initial, relevant_chronology)
@test ev.trajectory == ev_reduced.trajectory ;
@test ev.history == ev_reduced.history ;
```

However we want to compute the `LFE` in a robust and correct manner. We work with the `relevant_chronology`. We compute the `cremoval_fence`, which records the highest `infectee`
field encountered so far. Any feasible evolution cannot drop below this fence.
```{julia}
removal_fence =
    accumulate(max, z isa CRemoval ? z.target : 1 for z in relevant_chronology)
println(removal_fence)
```

We now want to work backwards through the `relevant_chronology`, 
commencing with a `current_timeline` set to the final value of the `removal_fence`,
at each step carrying over
the `AbstractIncident` `z` to a reverse `LFE` and tracking the new `current_LFE` level if either

 * `z` is a `CRemoval`, in which case the `current_LFE` level is unchanged and `z` is added to
`reverse_LFE`, or
 * an `OperativeInfection` for which the `infectee` field equals the `current_LFE` level 
 and _additionally_ the `current_LFE` level strictly exceeds the current value of the `removal_fence`.
 In this last case the `current_LFE` level is then decremented by `1`.
 * Otherwise nothing is done!
 
```{julia}
current_timeline = removal_fence[end]
rf2              = removal_fence[end]               # DIAGNOSTIC
reverse_LFE = AbstractIncident[]
@debug "fence\tline\tIncident"
for (z, rf) in Base.Iterators.reverse(zip(relevant_chronology, removal_fence))
    @debug "$rf\t\t$current_timeline\t\t$(sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), z))"
    if z isa CRemoval
        push!(reverse_LFE, z)
    elseif z isa OperativeInfection && z.infectee == current_timeline && current_timeline > rf
        push!(reverse_LFE, z)
        current_timeline -= 1
    end
    rf2 = rf                                        # DIAGNOSTIC
end
@debug "$rf2\t\t$current_timeline\t\tCOMPLETION"
```
```{julia}
LFE = reverse(reverse_LFE)
println(sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), LFE))
println(sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), ev.LFE))
```

```{julia}
@test CEvolution(initial, LFE).history == LFE ;
```

Implementation of `last_feasible_evolution`
-------------------------------------------
Here is a function which encapsulates the above work.
Note that it does not assume `ev.infections` to have 
been categorized as `OperativeInfection` versus `InOperativeInfection`.
```{julia}
function last_feasible_evolution(duration::Real, 
    ev::AbstractEvolution, iv::Innovation) ::Vector{AbstractIncident}
    
    @debug "Compute mixed chronology, recomputing `cremovals`"
    @debug "   and converting previous `OperativeInfection`s to `PInfection`s"
    @debug "   (perhaps there should be a mechanism to inherit this from calling code?)."
    recomputed_cremovals = EpidemicsCFTP.resulting_cremovals(ev, iv) 
    previous_history = [PInfection(z) for z in ev.chronology if z isa OperativeInfection]
    chronology = sort(iv.infections ∪ previous_history ∪ recomputed_cremovals)
    
    @debug "Compute `removal_boundary` and `relevant_chronology`"
    removal_boundary =
        accumulate(+, z isa CRemoval ? 1 : 0 for z in chronology, init=initial.r)
    raw_chronology = [z isa OperativeInfection && z.target ≤ rb ? KilledInfection(z) : z
            for (z, rb) in zip(chronology, removal_boundary)]
    relevant_chronology =
        filter(z -> !(z isa KilledInfection), raw_chronology)
    
    @debug "Compute `removal_fence`"
    removal_fence =
        accumulate(max, z isa CRemoval ? z.target : 1 for z in relevant_chronology)
    @debug "$removal_fence"
    
    @debug "Work backwards through `relevant_chronology`"
    current_timeline = removal_fence[end]
    rf2              = removal_fence[end]               # DIAGNOSTIC
    reverse_LFE = AbstractIncident[]
    @debug "fence\tline\tIncident"
    for (z, rf) in Base.Iterators.reverse(zip(relevant_chronology, removal_fence))
        @debug "$rf\t\t$current_timeline\t\t$(sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), z))"
        if z isa CRemoval
            push!(reverse_LFE, z)
        elseif z isa OperativeInfection && z.infectee == current_timeline && current_timeline > rf
            push!(reverse_LFE, z)
            current_timeline -= 1
        end
        rf2 = rf                                        # DIAGNOSTIC
    end
    @debug "$rf2\t\t$current_timeline\t\tCOMPLETION"
    
    return reverse(reverse_LFE)
end ;
```

Here are results from the first ten steps in algorithmic time.
```{julia}
for i in 1:10
    iv = generate_innovation(iv_null, duration, α=α, β=β)
    proposed_LFE = last_feasible_evolution(duration, ev, iv)
    
    ev = CEvolution(ev, iv)
    
    println("STEP $i")
    println("CREMOVALS ", sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), ev.cremovals))
    println("CURRENT   ", sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), ev.LFE))
    println("PROPOSED  ", sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), proposed_LFE))
    @test CEvolution(initial, ev.LFE).history == ev.LFE ;

    ev_previous = ev
end
```
